title: model-variant-selection-cost-latency-tradeoff-matrix-2024
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview
--------
This document defines a practical matrix and operational playbook for selecting model variants at routing time to balance per-request latency, unit cost, and end-to-end quality. It is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and product owners who operate the routing and fallback layers of the serving runtime.

Goals
- Provide a compact, auditable representation (the Variant Selection Matrix) that maps request classes to candidate model variants and their tradeoffs.
- Define telemetry and SLOs required to validate selection choices in production.
- Provide rollout and rollback playbooks for changing variant mappings.
- Give examples of automation hooks (autoscaler, router) that consume the matrix.

Intended audience and ownership
- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime (routing subgroup)
- Secondary: eng-sre, eng-platform, product (API performance)

Key definitions
- Model variant: a served artifact, e.g., llama-2-13b-q4_0, redwood-clarity-3-small-int8, or gptx-16k-fast. Includes quantization/precision, max-seq, and kernel-profile tags.
- Request class: a classification computed at the edge or ingress that captures latency sensitivity, token budget, and quality requirement (e.g., chat-low-latency, batch-embed, long-seq-generation).
- Unit cost: a normalized per-token cost metric that includes GPU time, memory amortization, and software overhead (expressed in microcost units).
- Latency budget: 95th percentile target for end-to-end generation for the request class.

The Variant Selection Matrix (VSM)
- The VSM is a table (stored as a JSON/YAML in the config store) mapping request_class -> ordered list of candidate variants with annotations. The router evaluates candidates in order and will fall back according to configured policies.

Example matrix (ASCII table excerpt)
+----------------------+-----------------------------+----------------+----------------+----------------------+
| request_class        | candidate_variant           | est_latency_ms | est_unit_cost   | quality_delta_pts    |
+----------------------+-----------------------------+----------------+----------------+----------------------+
| chat-low-latency     | redwood-clarity-3-small-i8  | 120            | 1.0            | -0.5                |
|                      | llama-2-13b-q4_0            | 230            | 0.75           | +0.4                |
|                      | redwood-clarity-3-medium-i8 | 180            | 1.3            | +0.7                |
+----------------------+-----------------------------+----------------+----------------+----------------------+
| batch-embed          | embed-compact-512           | 60             | 0.12           | N/A                 |
|                      | embed-accurate-1536         | 220            | 0.45           | +2.1                |
+----------------------+-----------------------------+----------------+----------------+----------------------+

Notes on table fields
- est_latency_ms: median token-generation time under representative load on dedicated pool. Populate from benchmarking suite.
- est_unit_cost: normalized units; derived from per-GPU time and amortized infra cost.
- quality_delta_pts: expected performance change on key evals (positive means better). Put ‘N/A’ for metrics not applicable.

How the router consumes the VSM
1) At request ingress, compute request_class (deterministic classification using prompt heuristics and headers).
2) Query config store for VSM entry for that class.
3) Evaluate candidate variants in order; for each candidate:
   - Check capacity availability in target pool (via allocator API).
   - Validate current observed 95p latency for the variant vs. request_class latency budget (from recent telemetry window).
   - If variant passes both, route request and annotate trace with variant_id, decision_reason=primary.
4) If no candidate passes, consult the fallback policy: either queue (short delay), route to best-effort low-cost variant, or proxy to Hosted API with higher SLA.

SLOs and telemetry required
- Per-variant 95p token-latency per request_class. Tag with variant and request_class.
- Per-variant per-1m throughput and active sessions.
- Per-variant quality regressions: daily evals on representative prompt sets, and online quality signals (e.g., rerank disagreement, human QA hits).
- Cost burn rate per-variant aggregated to product/unit.
- Decision coverage: fraction of requests classified and matched in VSM (target > 99%).

Benchmarking inputs and methodology
- Use the microbenchmark harness from benchmarking-and-perf-suite to produce: median/95p per-token latency under 1, 5, 10, 20 concurrent streams; memory footprint; kernel occupancy profiles.
- For quality deltas, run the curated eval suites from prompt-sets-and-benchmarks with at least 3 random seeds; report mean and 95% CI.
- Unit cost computed as: (GPU-ms * gpu_price + infra_overhead) / tokens_generated. Keep calculation script in /ops/costing/vsm_cost_calc.py and reference in the matrix metadata.

Rollout and change playbook (stepwise)
1) Author a matrix change PR: update YAML in config repo with rationale, benchmarking snapshots, and expected impact.
2) Automated preflight: run smoke simulations with sample workload in canary cluster (script: infra/tools/vsm_simulator.sh).
3) Canary deploy: enable new mapping for 1% traffic, observe these metrics for 2 hours: 95p latency, error rate, quality_signal, and cost burn.
4) Ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with 30–60 minute hold windows.
5) If any SLO regresses beyond thresholds (95p latency +20% absolute or quality delta <-1.0 on eval), rollback to previous matrix and open a production incident.

Rollback and incident triggers
- Immediate rollback triggers: error rate > 0.5% absolute increase, OOM or GPU watch-dog nodes thrown, or quality alerts (manual QA or automated threshold).
- Soft triggers: cost burn > expected by 30% for sustained 4h; treat as investigation item, may not trigger rollback automatically.

Operational knobs exposed to oncall
- emergency_variant_overrides: per-customer or per-route pin to a specific variant.
- degraded_mode: route all low-priority request_classes to minimal-cost variants.
- admission_timeout_ms: how long router will attempt to match before falling back.
- sampling_ratio: fraction of routed requests to sample for quality telemetry.

Example VSM YAML snippet (consumed by router)
---
request_classes:
  chat-low-latency:
    latency_budget_ms: 200
    candidates:
      - variant: redwood-clarity-3-small-i8
        note: fast-default
      - variant: redwood-clarity-3-medium-i8
        note: higher-quality
      - variant: llama-2-13b-q4_0
        note: cost-optimum
  batch-embed:
    latency_budget_ms: 1000
    candidates:
      - variant: embed-compact-512
      - variant: embed-accurate-1536
...

Telemetry example queries (Prometheus / SQL)
- 95p latency by variant/request_class: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, variant, request_class))
- Cost burn per variant (1h): sum(rate(gpu_ms_total[1h])) by (variant) * price_index

Testing and validation matrix (pre-merge checklist)
- [ ] Benchmarks attached for each candidate (median/95p and memory).
- [ ] Quality deltas for key evals are provided and annotated.
- [ ] Canary simulation passed with 0 incidents in automated run.
- [ ] Runtime telemetry schema updated if new tags were introduced.

Known interactions and gotchas
- Kernel scheduling differences: low-precision quantized variants may have lower per-token latency but produce worse occupancy for mixed-length sequences, causing 95p surprises under bursty workloads. When adding such variants, force-run occupancy microbenchmarks.
- KV cache fragmentation: switching variants with incompatible KV key formats will cause cold cache penalties. Matrix entries should include kv_compatibility tags.
- Cross-tenant memory eviction: heavy variants on shared pools can cause noisy-neighbor effects. Prefer dedicated pools or pool-quotas for heavy variants.

Release notes and auditability
- Every matrix change must be submitted as a PR and the PR description must contain: benchmark artifacts, telemetry snapshot (last 7d), and risk assessment. The config repo auto-tags changes and writes an audit entry to the change-log stream.

Related runbooks and pages
- See runtime runbooks for: emergency_variant_override, kvcache-consistency, and graceful-fallback-runbook. Links: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/session-lifecycle-kvcache-consistency-guidelines-2024
- See benchmarking suite: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/throughput-latency-workload-catalog-2026

Appendix A: Short decision record
- Decision: Model selection should prioritize latency budget for low-latency request_classes and cost for batch/throughput request_classes.
- Rationale: Product teams require predictable tail latency for chat experiences; batch embedding customers are more price-sensitive.
- Owner: routing subgroup (eng-serving-runtime)

Appendix B: Example incident timeline (summary)
1) 2025-01-17 03:12 UTC: Canary roll from 5% to 20% for chat-low-latency mapping to llama-2-13b-q4_0.
2) 03:28 UTC: 95p latency for chat-low-latency increased from 190ms -> 320ms.
3) 03:30 UTC: Automated rollback to previous matrix (clarity small-i8). Incident created: IR-2025-0117-variant-latency.
4) Postmortem: kernel occupancy for llama-2-13b-q4_0 at target concurrency was 40% vs. expected 72%; microbenchmarks had been run at lower concurrency.

Appendix C: Suggested experiments
- A/B traffic split experiments where 0.5% of requests are shadowed to a new variant and offline-quality is measured before enabling live traffic.
- Pressure testing: run burst tests with 10x typical concurrency to evaluate 95p degradation modes.
